viewer.info.title: Human Digestive System
viewer.info.description: The human digestive system includes the gastrointestinal tract plus accessory digestive organs.
viewer.info.details.overview: The human digestive system includes the gastrointestinal tract plus accessory digestive organs (the tongue, salivary glands, pancreas, liver, and gallbladder). In this system, digestion has many stages and begins first in the mouth (oral cavity). Digestion involves breaking food down into smaller components that can be absorbed and assimilated into the body. Saliva helps make food swallowable so it can pass through the esophagus and enter the stomach.
viewer.info.details.digestionAbsorption: Food enters the gastrointestinal tract and undergoes digestion, the process of breaking large food molecules into smaller molecules. However, small nutrient molecules must leave the digestive system and enter the body before they can be used. This is completed by a second process called absorption, when food molecules pass through the plasma membranes of the small intestine into the blood.
viewer.info.details.tract: Digestion occurs in the gastrointestinal tract, or digestive tube, which extends from the mouth to the anus.
viewer.info.details.parts: The digestive system is divided into parts, with each part adapted to its own function. The digestive tube includes the mouth, pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anal canal, and anus. Associated structures include the teeth, lips, cheeks, tongue, salivary glands, pancreas, liver, and gallbladder.
viewer.info.details.layers: Parts of the gastrointestinal tract have specialized functions, but all are made from the same basic tissue layers. From inside to outside, the wall of the tube includes the mucosa, submucosa, muscular layer, and serosa.

viewer.organ.daDay.name: Stomach
viewer.organ.daDay.description: The stomach is a J-shaped digestive organ located between the esophagus and small intestine. It secretes acid and enzymes to break down food into a liquid form.
viewer.organ.thucQuan.name: Esophagus
viewer.organ.thucQuan.description: The esophagus is a muscular tube connecting the throat to the stomach, transporting food via peristalsis.
viewer.organ.ruotNon.name: Small Intestine
viewer.organ.ruotNon.description: The small intestine is the longest part of the digestive tract where most digestion and nutrient absorption occurs.
viewer.organ.ruotGia.name: Large Intestine
viewer.organ.ruotGia.description: The large intestine absorbs water and electrolytes from digested food, forming and eliminating feces.
viewer.organ.gan.name: Liver
viewer.organ.gan.description: The liver is the largest internal organ, responsible for filtering blood, producing bile, metabolizing nutrients, and detoxification.
viewer.organ.tuiMat.name: Gallbladder
viewer.organ.tuiMat.description: The gallbladder is a small pear-shaped organ that stores and concentrates bile produced by the liver for fat digestion.
viewer.organ.tuy.name: Pancreas
viewer.organ.tuy.description: The pancreas functions as both an endocrine (insulin) and exocrine (digestive enzymes) gland, critical for digestion and blood sugar regulation.
viewer.organ.mieng.name: Mouth
viewer.organ.mieng.description: The mouth begins digestion by chewing food and mixing it with saliva before it moves into the esophagus.
